117607.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Georgia
117607.note: The Atlanta Jewish Times (CrownHeights.info, 9 Oct 2007, 'The Rebbe's Minyan'): 'When Rabbi New arrived in what is now the city of Sandy Springs in 1984 ... he set up the only Chabad center in Georgia, dubbed Chabad of Georgia'; also 'since Rabbi Yossi New arrived 23 years ago in an area where Chabad had failed to establish a foothold more than a decade earlier'. Chabad.org (CrownHeights.info, 9 Sept 2014): 'It's been 30 years since Rabbi Yossi and Dassie New first arrived in Atlanta'; '"It was 1984 ..."'. Its synagogue is Congregation Beth Tefillah, Sandy Springs.

118230.name: Chabad Intown
118230.note: The Atlanta Jewish Times (CrownHeights.info, 9 Oct 2007): 'Rabbi Schusterman, who established the center in 1997 and still leads it'; 'the center began on the second floor of Congregation Anshi S'fard in Virginia-Highland after he set up Chabad on Campus'; 'Chabad found a larger space in April 2000 on Ponce de Leon Avenue'. Today at 730 Ponce De Leon Place NE (whether that is the 2000 building is not stated). Rabbi Eliyahu and Dena Schusterman.

earlier.where: second floor of Congregation Anshi S'fard, Virginia-Highland

118608.name: Chabad at Emory
118608.note: The Atlanta Jewish Times (CrownHeights.info, 9 Oct 2007): 'Rabbi Eliyahu Schusterman, who heads Chabad Intown, started the campus branch on a part-time basis in 1997. When it went full time in 2000, Chabad barely had enough students for Rosh Hashanah services' (Rabbi Zalman Lipskier, its director since).

118208.name: Chabad of Augusta
118208.note: CrownHeights.info, 18 Nov 2022: 'In 1996, the first Chabad center was established by Rabbi Zalman and Chani Fischer, to serve the needs of the Jewish community. Fast forward 26 years'. Agreeing: the Atlanta Jewish Times (9 Oct 2007): 'Augusta has had a Chabad center for more than a decade. Going into his 12th year as the full-time founding rabbi, Zalman Fisher'. In 2022 Rabbi Mendel and Sarah Fischer joined.

531722.name: Chabad Israeli Center
531722.note: The Atlanta Jewish Times (CrownHeights.info, 9 Oct 2007): 'The Chabad Israeli Center recently opened in Sandy Springs. Lead by Rabbi New's son-in-law, Rabbi Mendy Gurary'. Today at 4276 Chamblee Dunwoody Road.

307665.name: Chabad of Athens-UGA
307665.note: Chabad.org (CrownHeights.info, 9 Sept 2014): Rabbi Michoel Refson: 'The first week we hosted Shabbat dinner when we arrived in 2005, we had four students around the table'. Agreeing: Chabad.org, 1 May 2008: the 'three-year-old' Chabad House; 'When they arrived to the school three years ago'. Its own center (279 Meigs Street) was due to open in fall 2008.

6500282.name: CMCH Elementary
6500282.note: Chabad.org (CrownHeights.info, 9 Sept 2014): Rabbi Isser New 'in 2010, the year the first- through sixth-grade Montessori-style elementary school first started'; 'it is now starting its fifth year, with 52 students'. The Chaya Mushka Children's House elementary school of Chabad of Georgia. Its chabad.org listing (6500282) is a new one, from about 2024.

527027.name: Kennesaw Chabad Jewish Center
527027.note: Began as the Chabad Jewish Center of Acworth. CrownHeights.info, 4 Feb 2008: Rabbi Zalman and Nechami Charytan 'have recently moved on Shlichus to Acworth, GA where they have established the Chabad Jewish Center of Acworth serving the Jewish residents of North West Cobb County'; Chabad.org, 23 Nov 2008: the Charytans 'established the Chabad-Lubavitch Jewish Center of Acworth, Ga., this year'. But the Atlanta Jewish Times (9 Oct 2007) said they would arrive 'in November' 2007, so they may have moved in late 2007: medium. Today at 3590 Frey Lake Road NW, Kennesaw (when it moved is not stated).

earlier.where: Acworth (the Chabad Jewish Center of Acworth)

117893.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Cobb County
117893.note: About 1991. The Atlanta Jewish Times (CrownHeights.info, 9 Oct 2007): Rabbi Ephraim Silverman, 'Since landing in Cobb County in 1999, eight years after Chabad opened there'. The Atlanta Journal-Constitution (CrownHeights.info, 26 Jan 2006): 'The congregation of Chabad of Cobb started with only a few families in the early 1990s. They met regularly to worship in a rented classroom and later in a storefront of a converted bakery in an east Cobb shopping center. In 1995, they bought a 40-year-old house on Lower Roswell Road'; Silverman director since 2000. That house was torn down in 2006 for the new building (4450 Lower Roswell Road, finished about 2008); meanwhile it rented space in a shopping center on Johnson Ferry Road (AJT, 2007). The year is worked out, not stated: medium.

earlier.where: a storefront (a converted bakery) in an east Cobb shopping center
rented space in a shopping center on Johnson Ferry Road (while its Lower Roswell Road building was rebuilt)

118282.name: Chabad of North Fulton
118282.note: Its own page: 'Chabad of North Fulton was established in 1998 to serve as a center for Jewish life and education in North Fulton County'; 'From 1998-2008 we operated under the name "Chabad of Alpharetta"', renamed in January 2009 after Johns Creek and Milton were incorporated. The Atlanta Jewish Times (9 Oct 2007): Rabbi Hirshy Minkowicz 'is entering his ninth year along the new border between Alpharetta and Johns Creek'.

118517.name: The Chabad Enrichment Center of Gwinnett
118517.note: Its own About page: 'Since opening our doors in 2001, we have become the center for Jewish connection for hundreds of families.' Agreeing: the Atlanta Jewish Times (9 Oct 2007): Rabbi Yossi and Esther Lerman 'are entering their seventh year in Gwinnett'. In 2007 they bought land at Spalding and Crooked Creek drives in Norcross; today at 6251 Smithpoint Drive, Peachtree Corners.
